objective:
Deploy one contract: PondsideGuard, a standalone Uniswap v4 hook with no token and no pool of its own, on Robinhood Chain. It must be usable by anyone initializing a new pool with it on the PoolManager passed as a constructor argument (Robinhood Chain PoolManager 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951).
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to my wallet. Expose claimFees() that anyone may call to redeem claims to the recipient.
2. For the first 10 minutes after the pool opens, each wallet may buy at most 1.0% of the total supply in total; larger buys revert. Expose windowEndsAt() as a view.
3. Collect 1.0% of the ETH side of every swap into a jar held by the hook. Whenever the jar holds at least 0.1 ETH, anyone may call buyback() to buy the pool’s token from this pool with the whole jar and burn the bought tokens. The swap that fills the jar does not revert if the buyback fails. Expose buyback() that anyone may call and jar() as a view.
4. The owner may pause and unpause swaps. Liquidity can always be removed while paused. Expose pause() and unpause() for the owner and paused() as a view.
Owner 0x5Bff2a2FEcD1d6152676813b21346238733bEAB1 may only: pause and unpause swaps, through the functions named above. No other admin function, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from the pool’s token; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem.
Take the PoolManager as a constructor argument and enable only the callbacks the behavior above needs. The deployed address must carry the correct hook permission bits (mine a CREATE2 salt). Owner, if any, is $owner.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.
